newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi does not expect new U.S. attack against Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Saudi does not expect new U.S. attack against Iraq.

text.p: Saudi Defence Minister Prince Sultan bin Abdul-Aziz said on Sunday he did not expect a fresh U.S. strike against Iraq after Baghdad's announcement it would suspend its air defence attacks on U.S. and allies warplanes.
Asked if he expected a military confrontation between the United States and Iraq after the Iraqi move, Prince Sultan replied to reporters: "No. I do not think so."
Prince Sultan was speaking north of the Saudi capital Riyadh after laying the foundation stone on Sunday for the Prince Sultan medical complex.

Iraq said on Friday it would suspend its air defence attacks on U.S. and allied planes policing no-fly zones over southern and northern Iraq. There have been no reports of any Iraqi attacks since then.

U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry, touring Gulf Arab states to mobilise support against Iraq, left Bahrain on Sunday for Jeddah and U.S. officials said he would hold talks with King Fahd of Saudi Arabia.

The United States fired 44 cruise missiles at southern Iraq on September 3 and 4 in response to Iraq's military incursion into Kurdish-controlled northern Iraq in alliance with one Kurdish faction against another.
